title: Read a carrier's ship dates on any server

blocks.text: A carrier's nightly CSV export has a ship-date column, and the shop prints a line from it on each customer's receipt. A few cells from last night's file:
The carrier's software writes the month in English, three letters, sometimes in capitals. The receipt spells the date out in English, like `Shipped Wednesday 3 December 2031`.
The shop's servers run in several countries, and their container images don't agree on a default locale. One was set up with a German default last month.

items: `receiptDate(...)`: the date as the receipt spells it out.

blocks.text: Every server must read every cell the carrier writes and print the same receipt. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: cells with an English three-letter month are read as dates
a receipt line names the day and the year of the ship date
a server whose default locale is German reads the same cells and prints the same English receipt
the carrier's three-letter September is read
a month written in capitals is read
the receipt writes the weekday and the month in full

origin.section: Month and Day Names Come From a Locale, So Name One

concepts: Month and day names come from the formatter's locale, the JVM default when none is given; English locales disagree (Sep and Sept), Locale.ROOT has no full names, and parsing names is case-sensitive unless the formatter is built case-insensitive.
